claims.claim: REQ-01-018 resolves 'today' from Account.timezone, which is nullable, and states no fallback for a caller with no timezone set — unlike the codebase's own precedent for this exact column.

witness.detail: schema.prisma:37 'timezone String?'; specs/user-management/12-time-tracking.md:109 states the established convention: 'falling back to UTC when the account has no timezone set'; apps/api/src/reports/reports.service.ts:551 does 'caller.timezone ?? "UTC"'. REQ-01-018 gives no equivalent fallback.

claims.suggestedFix: State the fallback (e.g. UTC) for a caller whose Account.timezone is null, matching the convention already used for the same column elsewhere.

claims.claim: The organization-country write (REQ-01-033/034) says nothing about two admins racing to set/clear the country concurrently — no lock is stated and no line says a lock is unneeded.

witness.detail: Lines 292-315 describe the write and its refusals but never address a concurrent write.

claims.suggestedFix: One line: a plain UPDATE with last-write-wins is fine here since there is no compound invariant across the write, or state the lock if one is wanted.

claims.claim: The Known Gaps table says 'the amendment organization/03 already names: resolve the holiday set at submit time and store which holidays the request counted' — but organization/03 contains no such detail; it only says the fix is 'a separate future amendment to spec 09' with no description of resolving at submit time or storing which holidays counted.

witness.detail: grep -n 'submit time|store which|frozen|snapshot' specs/organization/03-holidays.md returns nothing; the only relevant sentences (lines 22, 359) say only 'a separate future amendment to spec 09'.

claims.suggestedFix: State the closing plan as this spec's own claim ('a future amendment to spec 09 would need to...') rather than attributing detail to organization/03 that it does not contain.
